overall_safety_summary: The scene is generally organized, but safety risks are present due to an open waste bin at floor level creating a tripping hazard and sharp knives stored loose in the cutlery drawer.

hazards.description: A waste bin or lower drawer is left open at floor level to the left of the user.
hazards.explanation: This creates a tripping or collision hazard in a confined kitchen workspace.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults have a higher risk of falls and serious injuries from tripping over low-lying, unexpected obstacles.
hazards.recommended_action: Close the lower bin or drawer fully to keep the floor area clear of obstructions.

hazards.description: Sharp kitchen knives are stored loose and unsheathed inside the cutlery drawer compartments.
hazards.explanation: Reaching into a drawer with exposed blades increases the risk of accidental cuts and puncture wounds.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Age-related thinning of the skin and reduced manual dexterity make older adults more vulnerable to severe cuts from loose blades.
hazards.recommended_action: Use protective blade sheaths or a dedicated knife block instead of storing sharp knives loose in a drawer.

uncertainties: The exact contents and state of the lower open bin or drawer on the left.
